comments.author: nrp
comments.textRawHtml:
I’m digging into this with the team, along with comments in this post. Longevity has to include a streamlined and effective support experience in addition to the hardware being repairable.

There are several changes we made earlier this year to drastically shorten the number of back-and-forths to issuing replacement parts when submitting a support request, and we’re working to streamline that further. We’re also improving the RMA->quality->engineering pipeline to make sure we capture learnings and make fixes from field failures.

children.author: illiac786
children.textRawHtml:
I’ll say what everyone here knows: It’s possible to keep support in house but it’s very expensive, compared with outsourcing to Bengaluru for example. It would make the prices even higher and might result in not having any customers left to respect.

I am not disagreeing on support quality, but the price is very steep and ultimately paid by the customers.

children.author: stavros
children.textRawHtml:
I much prefer ChatGPT to the average support person I've talked to. I emailed Huel a few months ago for an issue, with a hastily-written email that I regretted as soon as I sent it, because I knew the support person would get lost and it would take forever to solve my issue.

To my surprise, ChatGPT replied immediately with "When you said 'refund', I assume you meant 'discount', so I've taken the liberty of issuing you a new coupon, please use it for your next order and I'm sorry for the problem".

I was blown away, I fully expected four days of back-and-forth while I explain my issue with my discount code that wasn't working.

children.textRawHtml: For what it's worth, I haven't had any experiences with Framework personally, but I recently bought a machine from another Linux laptop vendor. Their support has been nothing short of excellent, going as far as pointing me to kernel patches that were already mainlined but had not yet reached my distro of choice. So I don't think people NEED to be treated like dummies by default, especially when not operating at, say, HP's scale.

children.author: Affric
children.textRawHtml:
Yep.

Often enough customers are wrong about the root cause and their insight into fixing the problem is fairly shallow.

But knowing how you’ve treated them will make everything easier regardless. And your coworkers in any kind of service role are almost adversarial. If they weren’t incompetent you wouldn’t be dealing with a repeat customer.

When the customer is correct all along and you’ve exponentially increased how badly you’ve treated them.

children.author: scottmcmac
children.textRawHtml:
I'll just offer that I bought a Framework 13 ~4 months ago to replace a Lenovo laptop that had been flaky from the jump. Lenovo support was frustrating and useless helpping with the USB-C ports constantly dropping connectivity (I suspect a design flaw and overheating nearby) on the still in warranty laptop. So, in my n=1, the big guys support isn't great either.

So far, I'm happy with my Framework purchase... but haven't needed any support yet.

children.author: notnullorvoid
children.textRawHtml:
Lenovo support is atrocious. 3 months to get a laptop fixed isn't great, but it took Lenovo over 1 year to fix my broken on arrival thinkpad. 80+ hours (conservative estimate) of talking to their support staff over the phone, and many times shipping the machine to them, only to have it come back with the same issue or a new issue. Honestly with the time it took to get the laptop fixed it would've made more sense just to throw the thing in the trash and do some extra contact work.

I can't imagine how frustrating the experience would've been had I not had another machine to use for work.

Also their business practices seem extremely sketchy to me, one of the first things I asked when it arrived broken was if I could return it for a refund. They refused claiming that the return window had expired, and the window does not start when you receive the item, but instead when you order it (it took ~4 months after order to ship to me).

It was a real learning experience. Now I record every support conversation I have.

children.author: tredre3
children.textRawHtml:
Lenovo phone/email/chat tech support is indeed horrible to the point of being useless.

If you want actual support for your thinkpad, you need to pay the premium for on-site support. The pricing for 1-2 years is usually not that bad (relative to the price of a moderate thinkpad). The techs are hit or miss, but at least they come to your place with the parts (sometimes requiring 2 visits but it beats sending the laptop away for weeks/months).
